findings.evidence: `code/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/Kernel.lean:94` has `@[simp] theorem ker_toIdeal ... : (ker f hf).toIdeal = RingHom.ker ... := rfl`; the new lemma at lines 86-92 proves itself by `rw [quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_apply]`.
findings.fix: Remove this lemma, or replace the preceding API with the single preferred kernel spelling if callers really need that normal form.
findings.issue: `quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_apply_ringHomKer` is only a duplicate spelling of `quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_apply`: the changed quotient type uses `RingHom.ker`, but `(ker f hf).toIdeal` is already definitionally that kernel.

findings.evidence: Lines 96-102 and 106-112 have the same arguments and target; the latter is proved only by `rw [quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_symm_apply]`.
findings.issue: `quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_ringHomKer` is a second name for exactly the same signature and conclusion as `quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_symm_apply`, so it creates duplicated API with no more general statement.

summary: The main equivalence and compatibility statements are at the expected level, but the PR adds duplicate normalized-kernel lemmas instead of relying on the existing definitional kernel API.
